outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Sequence Modeling and the Rise of LSTMs
outline.description: This chapter sets the historical stage for the paper by reviewing the evolution of sequence modeling. It covers the fundamental challenges faced by early Recurrent Neural Networks (vanishing gradients), introducing the seminal innovations of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM): the Constant Error Carousel and gating mechanisms. Students will understand why LSTMs dominated natural language processing prior to 2017 and identify the specific architectural bottlenecks that led to their displacement by Transformers.
subtopics: Historical Context: From Vanilla RNNs to LSTMs
The Vanishing Gradient Problem and Solutions
Core Mechanisms: Cell States, Forget Gates, Input Gates, and Output Gates
Success Stories: Applications of LSTMs in RL, Translation, and Generation
The Three Critical Limitations of Standard LSTMs:

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Diagnosing Architectural Bottlenecks in Standard LSTMs
outline.description: Building on Chapter 1, this chapter rigorously analyzes the three primary failure modes of traditional LSTMs that prevent them from competing with modern Transformers at scale. Using conceptual examples like 'Nearest Neighbor Search' and 'Rare Token Prediction,' students will grasp why fixed scalar memories and rigid sequential dependencies hinder performance. This analysis serves as the motivation for every modification introduced in xLSTM.
subtopics: (i) Inability to Revise Storage Decisions (The Nearest Neighbor Problem)
(ii) Limited Information Capacity (Scalar vs. Rich Representations)
Why These Limitations Enabled the Shift to Self-Attention

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Core Innovation I - Exponential Gating and Stabilization Techniques
outline.description: This chapter dives into the mathematical foundations of the first major extension in xLSTM: Exponential Gating. Unlike standard sigmoids, exponential activations allow gates to take any positive real value, enabling dynamic revision of memory contents. Crucially, this section teaches how to handle numerical instability caused by exponentials through normalization states ($n_t$) and stabilizing logarithmic tricks ($m_t$).
subtopics: From Sigmoid to Exponential Activation Functions
Proof Preservation of Network Outputs under Transformation
How Exponential Gating Solves Static Storage Problems
